correctness.rationale: Normalized exhaustive finite proof: for each k=2..8 all C(L_k,k−1) sets with min=0 and span<=L_k are visited, where L=(1,3,6,11,17,25,34). Every t from 2k−1 to k(k+1)/2 is witnessed within its limit, so no smaller-diameter unexamined set can exist. Two independent exact programs enumerate 5,563,258 sets each, agree at every minimum; all witnesses checked. The only descent is d_8(32)=20 to d_8(33)=19. Primary bitset supports sums up to 68 without shift overflow; independent integer occurrence array supports all sums. A reproducible verifier checks the counts.

originality.rationale: The full inverse diameter vector for each k through 8 and first strict monotonicity reversal at (8,32) were not identified in targeted mathematical literature or existing public research records. The known optimal eight-mark Golomb ruler settles d_8(36)=34 only, and Rajagopal determines attainable cardinalities without individual minima. The first monotonicity reversal at eight points (32 sums demand span 20 while 33 demand 19) is not implied by known range or Golomb endpoint results and gives a structural boundary for plausible monotonicity heuristics.
